caseStudies.title: Cutting ADM Penalties with an Automated Booking Cancellation Service
caseStudies.description: A background service that automatically cancels un-ticketed bookings before the last ticketing time, saving ~$23K-$27K across 6 OTA clients.
caseStudies.body:
## The Problem

Airlines charge Agency Debit Memo (ADM) penalties when a travel agency holds a booking past the last ticketing time without issuing a ticket. Across the OTA platforms I supported, un-ticketed bookings were slipping past their deadlines because there was no automated way to catch and cancel them in time — someone had to notice and act manually, and that didn't scale across 6 client platforms.

## The Solution

I built a background service using **ASP.NET Core** and **Hangfire** that continuously monitors bookings approaching their last ticketing time. When a booking is still un-ticketed as the deadline closes in, the service automatically cancels it — removing the ADM exposure without requiring manual intervention. The job scheduling and retry behavior are backed by **SQLite** for lightweight, reliable persistence across restarts.

Key design points:

- Runs as a recurring Hangfire job, independent of the main booking API's request/response cycle
- Idempotent cancellation logic so re-runs or retries never double-cancel or corrupt booking state
- Configurable per-client thresholds, since each OTA's ticketing deadlines and airline agreements differ slightly

## The Results

- Reduced ADM penalties by **$4,500–$6,400 per month per OTA**
- Total savings of **~$23,000–$27,000** across 6 client platforms
- Removed a manual, error-prone monitoring step from the operations workflow entirely
